name: Positivism
summary: Positivism, as a political doctrine, is Auguste Comte's programme for rebuilding society on scientific knowledge after the French Revolution. It joins a philosophy and a polity: a spiritual power of thinkers and women guiding opinion by counsel and moral education, separate from a concentrated temporal power, with duties replacing rights, property treated as a social function under moral control, and a provisional popular dictatorship until the spiritual reorganisation is done. It rejects popular sovereignty, communism and class conflict, and ends in a Religion of Humanity built on living for others.
scope: Comtean positivism as a political doctrine, as the Stanford Encyclopedia says Comte's positivism is 'not a philosophy of science but a political philosophy': Comte's System of Positive Polity (1851-1854) and its summary, A General View of Positivism (1848). Answers follow Comte's mature doctrine. Logical or neo-positivism, which the same source says took over the name in the philosophy of science, and general scientific method are excluded, as are later movements such as Brazilian positivism. Where Comte's texts state no position, the answer is null.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: He holds that the separation of functions is a feature no less essential than their co-operation and that individuality cannot be dispensed with.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He treats the abolition of royalty, the last remnant of caste, as irrevocable and condemns aristocratic self-seeking, though he defends inheritance of property.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: He says the intervention of society is necessary in marriage, to confirm and develop the natural order, and that it must be exclusive and indissoluble.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Comte keeps wages paid in money in his normal state, proposes a common coinage, and says the existing wage plan suits direct services.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He says government will still have to repress by force the more dangerous class of delinquencies, and notes that the police protect people daily.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: He says the workman need not be paid by the State instead of a private employer and that the present wage plan suits direct services; wages stay, as the maintenance of each family.

bound-labor.rationale: He treats the liberty of the workman as what enables true moral unity and sees slavery and serfdom as stages to be left behind.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: In his provisional government the assembly's duty would be to vote the budget proposed by the finance committee and audit the past year's accounts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: He holds that the people are incompetent to express opinions on difficult or indirectly applied questions and should adopt the opinion of superior officers who have their confidence.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He treats the voluntary renunciation of dominion over a non-western people as a mark of the shame of dominion, and Preparatory Government restores Algeria to the Arabs.

class-collaboration.rationale: Positivists present themselves as the party of construction who satisfy the Poor and restore the confidence of the Rich, with the spiritual power as supreme court of arbitration between workmen and employers.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Comte held that ideas, not material or class conflict, govern social order, and presents Positivism as the party of construction reconciling the classes.

clerical-rule.rationale: He requires the priesthood of Humanity to abandon any prospect of temporal power, parliamentary as well as administrative.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He limited the extent of states to small republics and proposed decomposing overgrown national aggregates, so a state claiming land beyond its borders because of nationality is rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: His Polity has the Preparatory Government restore Algeria to the Arabs and proclaim the independence of the French colonies.

common-currency.rationale: He proposes a common monetary standard for Western Europe, with the consent of governments, to facilitate industrial transactions.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He rejects popular sovereignty and denies that the choice of rulers should rest with the electorate, though he wants the people's support for government.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He holds that formal attempts to set up constitutions on an abstract ideal are futile and that the legislature should be reduced to voting the budget.

culture-before-state.rationale: He holds that spiritual reorganisation must precede political reconstruction, and that attempts at political reconstruction first are destructive.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He calls the white race superior in all its branches to the other two and speaks of populations whose growth has been retarded.

death-penalty.rationale: His Polity says the punishment of death can never be wholly disused for incorrigible natures and will become rarer, though it is inadmissible for political offences in the transitional government.

decide-locally.rationale: He holds, in opposition to revolutionary prejudices, that the central power should preponderate over the local, and sides with the central power in almost all cases.

democracy-best.rationale: Positivism rejects the Sovereignty of the People and refuses, as a rule, to submit political questions and the choice of rulers to incompetent judges.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He refuses to submit the choice of rulers to the electorate and has his provisional rulers drawn from the working class under the executive's ascendancy over the electoral body.

direct-votes.rationale: He says that for the people to take a direct part in government and decide political measures finally is adapted only to times of revolution.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He says equality of the sexes is contrary to their nature, that women should be excluded from political authority and passed over for inheritance, and that man should provide for woman.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He writes that rights are possible only while power is considered as emanating from a superhuman will, a theological conception he places in the past.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The most important object of his polity is the substitution of Duties for Rights, and he would exclude the word Right from political language.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He treats royalty as the last remnant of caste and its abolition as irrevocable.

elective-rulers.rationale: He refuses, as a rule, to submit the choice of rulers to judges who are obviously incompetent.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He calls the rights of Man an anti-social conception useful only for destruction and would exclude the idea of Right entirely, and he considers written constitutions futile.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He holds that in the Positive state rights in the ordinary sense can be claimed by none, so equal rights before the law is not his principle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Mixed: he condemns schemes that sacrifice liberty to 'uncontrolled equality' and keeps unequal wealth and rank, yet his normal state sets a uniform wage for all working families.

experts-over-public.rationale: He says the people are incompetent on difficult or technical questions and should adopt the opinion of superior officers, and gives guidance of society to a philosophic spiritual power.

family-wage.rationale: His Positive Polity sets wages as the maintenance of the workman's household of seven members, paid at a uniform rate for all families.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: He excludes women from political authority and public office, holding that their part is to moderate through the family and not to govern.

gender-social-construct.rationale: He holds that the differentiation of the sexes is natural and has grown with civilisation, and that equality in their position is contrary to their nature.

gradual-change.rationale: He says Positivism will mould institutions ultimately and by slow degrees, with at least a generation needed, and that modifying them too rapidly would cause fresh disturbances.

head-of-state-dissolves-parliament.rationale: His provisional triumvirate, combining the functions of ministry and monarchy, would convoke and dissolve the electoral power on its own responsibility.

history-own-civilization.rationale: He teaches history as that of Humanity as a whole and wants instruction and lectures to be Occidental rather than simply national.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Comte regarded the industrial society, replacing military ones, as the positive stage of society, according to the Stanford Encyclopedia.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: His normal plan decomposes overgrown national aggregates into Republics of one to three million, so uniting related peoples in one larger state runs against it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He holds that in the Positive state no supernatural claims are admissible and that law and order rest on demonstrable principles and moral education, not theology.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The Stanford Encyclopedia states that Comte strongly disagrees with historical materialism, holding that ideas rule the world.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He calls the abolition of monarchy the only irrevocable political point, since monarchy is the symbol of retrogression.

moral-incentives.rationale: He keeps wages as the recompense of work and adds social gratitude to them, so duty supplements material rewards without replacing them.

nation-first.rationale: He wants Western education and associations to be Occidental, not simply National, and measures common to the West placed beyond national rivalry.

national-church-status.rationale: He says no special set of principles should be placed under official patronage and that all official grants to theological and metaphysical institutions would be discontinued.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: He sees organic nature united under Humanity to develop all the resources of the planet, and says activity toward unassimilable animals is one of destruction.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: He holds that marriage must be both exclusive and indissoluble and blames Protestant divorce laws for impairing monogamy.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The spiritual power is to impose duties on capitalists toward their subordinates, and in the normal state the patriciate maintains the workers' households.

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: He calls monogamy one of the most precious gifts of the Middle Ages and requires the union to be exclusive.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He holds that the people's taking direct part in government and deciding political measures is suited only to times of revolution, and that most questions exceed their competence.

pay-for-effort.rationale: He holds that wages are a condition of existence and the means of action, not the price of labour, and sets a uniform rate for all families with differences only for the cost of living.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He says the well-being of the people should be the one great object of government and that the working class, because of its numbers and difficulties, requires special interference.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He says decisions of law courts and declarations of war should be announced in the name of the whole body politic, which keeps the courts as public bodies.

property-fundamental.rationale: The General View calls the modern jurists' view of property as an absolute right of the possessor an anti-social theory with no foundation in justice or fact, so property is not a right that is hard to override.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Comte treats proprietorship as a social function of creating and administering capital for the community, and says the true principle of republicanism is that all forces work together for the common good.

public-ownership.rationale: He rejects the Communists' practical solution of changing the mode of tenure, holding that industry needs its private captains and that property is to be regulated by moral rather than legal means.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: His provisional government would abolish all penalties and fines that hamper free speech and discussion, leaving only the obligation of signature.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He wants the use of wealth controlled by moral rules from the spiritual power, 'moral, not political in their source', leaving legal force for the more palpable delinquencies.

restore-past-order.rationale: He calls Positivism the party of construction, defines Progress as the development of Order, and condemns the retrograde school.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: He holds that refusal of co-operation is a power every free agent ought to be allowed on his own responsibility, to be regulated by the philosophic body and not forbidden by law.

return-to-foraging.rationale: His law of three stages presents the positive and industrial state as the normal state of humanity, with earlier stages as preparation.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He holds that in the Positive state no supernatural claims are admissible, so a head of state cannot be regarded as sacred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He values continuity with the past, criticising Communists and progressive schools for their anti-historic spirit and proposing commemoration of the dead.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Comte's ethical problem is the subjection of self-love to social love, with the maxim 'Live for Others'.

separate-church-state.rationale: He says spiritual power must be wholly independent of every kind of temporal power and that official grants to theological institutions should be discontinued.

separated-powers.rationale: Mixed: he makes the separation of spiritual from temporal power his principle but calls it an error to balance legislative against executive or local against central power.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: He holds that even within the family a woman's influence should be that of persuasion rather than command, and that man should provide for woman.

single-common-good.rationale: He writes that the true principle of republicanism is that all forces work together for the common good and rejects balancing powers against each other.

socialized-care.rationale: He makes the family the woman's sphere, her mission being the moral education of her children, with man maintaining her, so domestic work is not handed to public services.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He subordinates politics to morals and holds that social questions are solved by moral agencies of the spiritual power.

state-harmful.rationale: The General View states that temporal power will always be necessary and that government must repress delinquencies by force, though the spiritual power will modify its action.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He distinguishes Positivism from Atheism, which like Theology discusses insoluble mysteries, and wants no doctrine under official patronage.

strong-leader.rationale: He advocates a provisional popular dictatorship with a preponderant central authority, with the executive taking ascendancy over the electoral body.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He says spiritual power must be wholly independent of every kind of temporal power, whether central or local.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: He says the remedy for the evils of modern society must be almost entirely of a moral kind and that the primary social problems are moral rather than political.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Comte limited the extent of temporal power to small republics of one to three million people and proposed breaking up overgrown national aggregates.

total-state.rationale: He confines government to material order and keeps the spiritual power wholly independent, with education and opinion outside its control.

traditional-family.rationale: He treats the family as woman's principal sphere and conjugal love as the education for universal sympathy, upholding indissoluble monogamy and the domestic order.

unions-good.rationale: Mixed: the General View treats the right to suspend work as an ultimate resource every collective body must keep, while the Polity says public works are needed against unions' tendency to imperil industrial action.

universal-morality.rationale: He holds that Positive morality, based on Humanity, is superior to earlier moralities and every nation is destined for the same ultimate conditions of social regeneration.

unpaid-domestic-work-exploitation.rationale: He treats women's domestic life as their privilege and mission, with man bound to maintain them, so it is not exploitation.

war-builds-character.rationale: He calls the retrograde parties' regret for the decline of the military spirit foolish and puts industry's peaceful order in the place of war.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He calls it a waste of effort to rectify the distribution of material power and says concentrated capital under private leaders is what the spiritual power can hope to penetrate with a sense of duty.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: He holds that marriage must be indissoluble, so a wife could not end it on her own initiative.

women-distinct-values.rationale: He calls women the organ of Feeling and the sympathetic element of the spiritual power, abounding in sympathy.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: He states that women should not be allowed to inherit, since they are exempt from the labour of production and man is to maintain them.

women-suffrage.rationale: He says women's part is not to govern but to modify, that they must abstain from practical pursuits, and that they have been rightly excluded from political authority.

worker-ownership.rationale: He argues that no great works could be undertaken if each worker were also a director, and keeps the division between capitalist and workman as the germ of industrial organisation.

workers-councils.rationale: He holds that workers should not insist on political rights, that political power should as a rule be concentrated, and that their role is moral, as supporters of the spiritual power.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He argues industry cannot function if each worker is also a director or if management is entrusted to a passive and irresponsible body instead of being fixed.

missingStatements.text: Society needs a shared secular faith, centred on humanity rather than God, to hold it together.
missingStatements.rationale: Comte's Religion of Humanity was meant to give positivist societies the cohesion traditional worship gave.

missingStatements.text: Women's proper sphere is the family rather than public power.
missingStatements.rationale: Comte placed women's main sphere in the family and rejected modern claims of women's rights.

missingStatements.text: The state should leave education to bodies independent of it.
missingStatements.rationale: Comte holds that a general system of education presupposes a doctrine the state cannot supply, and that governments should abdicate the educational powers they hold, leaving education to private effort and later to the spiritual power.

quotes.text: no general system of State education should be attempted
quotes.where: General View, chapter II (Liberty should be extended to Education)

quotes.text: So far, then, from inviting government to organize education, we ought rather to exhort it to abdicate the educational powers which it already holds
quotes.where: General View, chapter III (We are not ripe for this system at present)

notes: Mill separated the 'good Comte' of the Course from the 'bad Comte' of the Polity; this profile follows the Polity, which holds the political doctrine. Followers such as George Eliot and Harriet Martineau kept altruism and a humanity religion but rejected much of the system, and Brazilian republicans drew on its order-and-progress motto. Later pass under rules 7 (the earlier audit predates the rules). Sources read in full text: the General View (Gutenberg), the four volumes of the System of Positive Polity (Internet Archive, Cornell copies), the Stanford Encyclopedia entry and Mill's essay; all saved in scratchpad/sources/positivism/. Wikipedia pages were dropped as sources. Every earlier answer was rechecked against Comte's texts: those his texts do not settle (including inferences from his rejection of laissez-faire or from the law of three stages, such as the statements on markets, taxes, inheritance, creationism, the Holocaust, tariffs and equal rights of groups) were nulled, and those he states were kept or changed with a cited passage. Themes searched without finding a position: healthcare, drugs, abortion, same-sex marriage, immigration, banking and central banks, taxation, trade, nuclear power, climate, AI and encryption, nationality law and the modern constitutional questions, which fall outside the 1848-1857 texts. Britannica's article was not used (blocked to scripted access). The Positive Polity's rules of morals and procreation (volumes 2 and 4) were skimmed, not exhaustively read.
